hints: Start at the vena cava and follow deoxygenated blood only on the right side of the heart toward the lungs, then cross off any left-side or systemic structures like the aorta, left atrium and pulmonary vein.

Remember blood can flow past electrical structures without flowing through them, so think of the order blood meets them in the right atrium wall, then between atria and ventricles, then in the ventricle wall, then at the ventricle exit.
walkthrough:
**Filter the list to the right-side pulmonary route**

Blood from the vena cava enters the right atrium, then right ventricle, then pulmonary artery to the lungs. So ignore left-side and systemic structures: aorta, left atrium and pulmonary vein are not on this route.

**Order the five structures blood meets or passes**

Think of the journey in order. First, blood enters the right atrium past the sinoatrial node in its wall. Second, it flows past the atrioventricular node between atria and ventricles. Third, it enters the right ventricle past the Purkyne tissue in the ventricle walls.

**Finish the exit to the lungs and count to third**

Fourth, blood is pumped out through the pulmonary semilunar valve. Fifth, it travels in the pulmonary artery to the lungs. Counting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the third structure is Purkyne tissue.

options.A: The atrioventricular node is second in this sequence, passed as blood moves from right atrium toward right ventricle, not third.
options.B: Purkyne tissue in the ventricle wall is passed after the two nodes and before the semilunar valve, so it is correctly third.
options.C: The semilunar valve is fourth, at the exit of the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery, not third.
options.D: The sinoatrial node is first, in the wall of the right atrium where vena cava blood first arrives, not third.
